lines.en: Today’s conquests in alphabetical order: Ayane.
That’s it.
After spending the bulk of yesterday spreading myself across the land like the worst version of Johnny Appleseed, I decided today should be a day of rest.

I figure that if I’m going to get called out by one of the most mild-mannered girls in school, the least I can do is cut back for twenty-four hours and only make love to the ones where it feels more passionate and less carnal.
Plus, Ayane was a little upset after breakfast too. And it appears that my semen may serve as some sort of medicine for her as she is mostly fine now that she’s been conquered.
Or is at least pretending to be fine — which essentially just is being fine by Ayane’s standards, so I’m not about to tell her how to live her life.
She will tell me how to live mine, though. That there’s another gathering in this very room beginning in about two hours. And how I won’t be able to have any more sex until tomorrow.
I don’t know if I could even if I wanted to, though. For she smiled in a way that no one else smiles just thirteen seconds before her biggest orgasm of the evening and it tore my sails in two.

And had she not already been immersed in the process of collapsing into my chest after each round of cowgirlish coitus, I’d have thought that it was her expression that knocked the wind out of me in that moment.
Upon reflection, I think it was. Because the thought of anyone else smiling like that makes me sick to my stomach. So she’ll remain in my head as the only one I’m willing to inflict that upon.
That won’t stop me from mentally undressing other girls, though. And as I step into the hall for a moment of fresh air, I happen upon two lungs full of black mold and a gag in my mouth.
: Hello.
: I take it you’re here to see me and not Ayane, right?
: I’m not sure. I just had a strange compulsion to stand outside of this door and wait for someone to exit. But I don’t know what to do now that you have.
: Well, have you talked to Makoto at all? Because right now she’s-
: She has informed me that I am potentially important and that my presence is required for a pajama-based meeting here in two hours.
: I think it’d be perfectly fine if you kept the swimsuit on. In fact, I’d go so far as to encourage it.
: I will consider this. But will my immaculate form not serve only to detract from the topics we are bound to discuss just a short while from now?
: It’ll be a pretty straight room, fortunately. I imagine any eyes on you other than mine will be of envy rather than lust.
: Tell me — if you are so attracted to me, why have we not had sexual intercourse yet?
: Uh-
: Is it because I am stronger than you and you are worried that I will take charge? Because you are likely correct.
: Tsuneyo, this...probably isn’t the place to just-
: Then let us go outside and talk about sexual intercourse there.
: What?
: Let us go outside and talk about sexual-
: I heard what you said. I just don’t understand why you suddenly want to talk about this when we’ve never even held hands before.
: Yet you have carried my naked body in your arms. Is such a thing not closer to the final stage of a relationship than hand-holding?
: Well, one is far more consensual than the other.
: Interesting. I had assumed consent was merely optional to adults and that you had not attempted to fuck me out of sheer politeness. And yes, I do speak of actual fucking this time.
: Uhh...well...it’s not optional. But is there a reason you’re being so forward about this all of a sudden?
: Recently, I attempted to tell you something only for my mind to be commandeered by what the Emerald Guardian would describe as an “unseen entity.”
: I would like to know why. And I believed engaging in similar conversation could potentially invoke such an experience again. So please, do your worst and fuck me right here.
: I remain unfucked. Will a term of endearment spur you to action, perhaps? Please have sex with me, bro.
: Tsuneyo, that’s not-
: Put it inside of me, big bro.
: ...Closer. Something’s still not right, though.
: I agree. Which is why I have decided to go through with such a heinous act in the first place. If I need to give up my autonomy to save my autonomy, so be it.
: And frankly, I am just not very good at masturbating. I have tried several times and it mostly just feels odd.
: How much of that...talk do you remember? The one where you told me about your...supernatural sex dream, for lack of a better term.
: Because I assumed it was sort of just...purged from your mind afterwards. Similar stuff happens to me sometimes when my thoughts are “commandeered.”
: But you’ve remembered things in the past that you probably shouldn’t have, so...maybe you’re special in some way.
: I am special in many ways. You are right to acknowledge this.
: In terms of what I remember, however, the details are still somewhat foggy.
: I recall stepping away from Tojo Ramen and walking with you. Then stopping near a spot that overlooks the town.
: I remember telling you about the dream. And then you being surprised. And then I believe my head started to hurt, but...
: The memories appear to cut off there.
: Have we already had sex and it was just so unremarkable that I didn’t bother to remember it?
: You’d remember it.
: I would hope so after all of the practice you have gotten. But you are mostly unimpressive in every other aspect of life, so I would not be shocked if this was any different.
: Insults aside, I’ve actually been wanting to talk to you about this too.
: I just...didn’t really know how since it all went by so quickly and I’m used to stuff like that just not even registering to anyone else.
: It’s been happening more often lately, though. And now it’s actually sticking for some people.
: Like Nao, for example. Just the other day, she and I got thrown into some weird...waiting room dimension thing and then spit back out like it was nothing. We both remember it too.
: And, come to think of it, she showed up not long after your mind broke that day. So maybe she’s somehow involved and just...not saying anything?
: I apologize for being the one to break this news to you, but Nao-chan is incapable of speaking.
: Nor do I believe she should be involved in conversations about sexual intercourse. But I understand that you are less opposed to the inclusion of children in such areas than I am.
: It’s worth thinking about at least, isn’t it?
: Again, I can not police what you do in your mind. But we are talking about mine right now, and there are no children present there.
: Please just tell me what happened next...where my memories cut out. And whether or not you subsequently defiled the temple that is my body.
: Hah...
: You weren’t really in any condition to be walking...and I wasn’t about to just leave you in the middle of the road, so I picked you up and carried you back to the ramen shop.
: Interesting. I am once again surprised you possess the strength to lift me at all.
: I tried calling out for your dad to see if he could, you know, come down and take you off of my hands. But when he didn’t respond, I assumed he was just too sick to.
: So I brought you upstairs myself — where that assumption subsequently changed into something else entirely.
: Customers are not allowed on the top floor of Tojo Ramen. How unfair that you have found a loophole to store policy by being present while I was undergoing demonic possession.
: Tsuneyo...don’t take this the wrong way or anything, but...
: Do you even have a father?
: I’m sorry?
: It’s just...there was nothing there. It was all just white apart from a single door that was blocked off. And when I tried to open it, you...
: Well? What did I do?
: Stripped naked and started begging me to have sex with you.
: In my own home?...
: When did I become such a whore?
: Tsuneyo...what the fuck is going on with your house? Why is it like that? What’s behind that door?
: Which door? There are several.
: There...was only one, I think. Apart from the one we entered from at least.
: But sure, assuming there was another I just didn’t see, what’s behind the one covered in caution tape?
: Caution tape?
: Yeah...What are you hiding in there? Why go to such lengths to block off something in your own home?
: Sensei — is it possible that your memories of that night have been somehow manipulated as well? Because what you’re describing doesn’t sound like my home at all.
: What? But then...
: Is it...possible your perception of that place is just warped entirely? Like...maybe you just started pretending to see it as something it’s not as some kind of...coping mechanism or-
: No, hold on. I’ve saved pictures of it since I would not allow the Emerald Guardian upstairs either and she wanted to know what it looked like.
: Here. This is the living room. It’s what you’ll see the moment you enter the home.
: What? That’s not-
: And this is where I sleep. My father is in the room beside mine and the restroom is to the right of his door.
: I...I don’t-
: I have learned from the Green Onion about an application called “FaceTime” recently. If you are that curious, I could call you from it and give you a more formal tour.
: All I ask is to omit my father’s room as I do not want to disturb him.
: But...all the white and...and the writing on the walls...
: What did...where was I then? I don’t understand...
: Perhaps you were experiencing another one of those moments you mentioned several minutes ago? Being pulled into a peculiar dimension for a short time?
: The Emerald Guardian has flagged me as a potential time traveler, so I believe I am an authority on interdimensional travel and am willing to lend some credibility to your cause.
: But it...felt so real...
: I can...still smell it...I can hear the sound of your voice echoing off the walls...Remember how blinding the fluorescent light was.
: But you can also remember the specifics of a place you have already confirmed to be fictitious, correct? The waiting room where you found a god?
: Yeah, but-
: Did I...
: Mention meeting a god there?
: Nao-chan! Cease the forward momentum of your youthful footarms!
: I am too unyoung to maintain up at this point!
: Nao...she’s here again.
: Friend? What are you doing here?
: Shouldn’t I be asking you that?...
: Why do the two of you keep popping up in the middle of everything weird lately? It’s like ever since Halloween, you’re practically at the forefront of it.
: Weird? What is weird? What does the mattering right now, Friend? Why are your eye mustaches angled in such a distrustful way?
: Whose idea was it to come here, Kaori?...Yours? Or Nao’s?
: It was Nao-chan’s idea. This is merely my attempt to facilitate her happiness as a devoted mothermom.
: Interesting. Let us hope that her appearance tonight does not predict yet another anomaly in our daily lives.
: What is “anomaly?” If Nao-chan did something wrong, please allow me to be the one to punish her. I do not trust the ramen girl.
: Trust is a two-way street and this road is closed. Be gone, spider woman. It’s my turn to get fucked.
: No one is doing any fucking right now.
: Darn.
: And while I do want to know why Nao was suddenly compelled to come to the beach just in time for more weird shit, I have a more important question for her first.
: Nao. Do you remember finding me upstairs in the ramen shop?
: Do you remember what it looked like?
: Kaori? What-
: Shh! My earmouths are feasting upon the sounds of her brainthoughts.
: Well?
: Nao-chan says it a was a traditional style 2LDK home that smelled faintly of pork broth and looked like it hadn’t been dusted in a long time.
: Nonsense. I dust it every other year.
: You don’t remember a white room, Nao?
: She remembers nothing of the sort.
: And what about Amber? Do you remember her?
: Yes.
: Huh...
Why is it just Tsuneyo’s house that eludes her then? Unless...
Unless I was the one perceiving it incorrectly. But what reason would I have to warp the state of her home into something so...sterile?
I’m probably dwelling on this a little too much. And it probably won’t change anything in the long run.
But little by little, more cracks in the fabric of reality keep showing up. So either the world is breaking, or I am. And neither of these things are good for any of us.
What can we do to fix it, though? Because just knowing something is broken doesn’t teach us how to do that.
And leaving things alone might break them even more, so the solution seems at first glance to just build more.
Can what we build really outpace the destruction of everything else, though? And, if it can’t, how long do we have left before we’re buried beneath the rubble of options never explored?
I’m not quite sure, to be honest.
But thinking so intensely about it works up an appetite.
